nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension $n$ with its standard Riemannian metric. For every real number $a$ and every $x \in F$, the Laplacian of the function $y \mapsto \frac{a}{2}\|y\|^2$ at $x$ is $a \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Laplacian of the Gaussian potential

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension $n$ with its standard Riemannian metric. For every $x \in F$, the Laplacian of the function $y \mapsto \|y\|^2$ at $x$ is $2n$.
nodes.title: Laplacian of the squared norm

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space with its standard Riemannian metric, let $f : F \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in F$, and let $Df$ denote the Fréchet derivative of $f$, taken to be $0$ at points where $f$ is not differentiable. Suppose $Df$ is differentiable at $x$, with derivative $D^2 f(x)$ there. Then the Laplacian $\Delta f(x)$ equals $\sum_i D^2 f(x)(b_i, b_i)$ for any orthonormal basis…
nodes.title: The Laplacian on a vector space is the flat Laplacian at twice-differentiable points

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension $n$ with its standard Riemannian metric, let $f : F \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in F$, and let $e_1, \dots, e_n$ be the orthonormal basis of the tangent space $T_xF$ used in the definition of the Laplacian, viewed as vectors of $F$. nodes.title: Laplacian on a vector space as a sum of second directional derivatives

nodes.summary: The Laplace-Beltrami operator applied to `f : M → ℝ` at `x`: `Δf(x)` is the metric trace `∑ i, hessian I f x (e i) (e i)` over the orthonormal basis `e = stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (TangentSpace I x)`, the same basis convention as `Manifold.scalarCurvature`. For the textbook Hessian, which is bilinear, this trace does not depend on the orthonormal basis; the regularity caveat of `Manifold.hessian` applies here unchanged.
nodes.title: Laplace–Beltrami operator

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
